newsitem.title: USA: Colonial Pipeline sets rebate to boost new service.
newsitem.headline: Colonial Pipeline sets rebate to boost new service.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline, drumming up interest in its new pipeline-to-barge transportation service, said it will offer some of its clients rebates if they make use of the company's bundled service.

Colonial plans to offer a 10-cent per barrel rebate to clients who move premium gasoline or distillates like diesel or heating oil on the pipeline and then onto barges to their final destination. The rebates do not cover jet fuel, the company said.

The deal, which involves parking the refined products in Colonial-provided tankage at Carteret, New Jersey before final barging to to New England, New York Harbor, or upstate New York, is valid between June 1 and September 30, Colonial said.

Additionally, over the same period period, Colonial will offer an 8-cent per barrel rebate to customers who simply move a minimum of four million barrels of premium gasoline or 150,000 barrels of distillates without any connection to the barging component of the main deal.
Colonial Pipeline, the largest refined products pipeline in America, is the main artery connecting the the Gulf Coast's "Refinery Row" to the populous Northeast.
It is owned by a consortium of 10 oil companies, and pumps a total of 2.1 million barrels per day of refined products.
